hypotheses.reasoning: notif-db disk on /var/lib/mysql climbed from 95% (22:24:13) to 99% (22:28:00) as binlog/WAL grew. At 22:29:51 InnoDB hit 'No space left on device' writing notifications.ibd. Right after that, notification-svc inserts began failing with 'table is full' (error 1114 / ER_RECORD_FILE_FULL). Those failures reach the gateway as POST /v1/notify 500s starting at 22:30:40. Reads stay healthy because only writes need disk space. I ruled out three other leads. The flag-sync unknown-flag errors are a staging-2 config issue, and the billing-reconciler checksum errors come from old archive partitions and began before onset. Neither touches the notify path. The auth-svc deploy came at 22:33, after the failures started.
Billing-reconciler checksum violations on archive rows. These are unrelated to the notify write path.
The auth-svc deploy came after the 500s had already started and did not touch notification writes.

verdict.recommendedAction: Free disk space on notif-db right away: purge or rotate old binlogs (PURGE BINARY LOGS) or expand the volume. Then check that inserts into notifications succeed again. After that, set binlog retention (binlog_expire_logs_seconds) and add disk alerts at 85% and 90%. Look into why binlog growth sped up (440 to 726MB/h).
